data.title: GitHub
data.description: Issues, branches, files and pull requests in the repositories you list, with every write read back from GitHub.

fields.name: token
fields.help: A fine-grained personal access token for the listed repositories.

auth.description: pat: a fine-grained token (credential kind bearer). app: a GitHub App (credential kind fields, private_key).

repos.description: 1 to 50 entries, owner/name or owner/*: the hard boundary.

protected_branches.description: Branch names or globs; default main, master, release/*.

issue_marker.description: Append <!-- deedglass:act_… --> to bodies Deedglass creates (default true).

data.summary: Issues, branches, files and pull requests in the repositories you list.

setup.title: Create a fine-grained token
setup.detail: Only the repositories you list, with Contents, Issues and Pull requests read and write. Or install a GitHub App.

setup.title: Store the token
setup.command: deedglass connector credentials set github --from-env GITHUB_SANDBOX_TOKEN

limits: Only the repositories in the config. Nothing outside them, including forks.
No repository settings, secrets, Actions runs or force pushes.
L1 shows GitHub's state, not whether the change was right.

tools.name: github.get_repo
tools.title: Get repo
tools.description: Read a repository's settings: visibility, default branch, description.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.list_issues
tools.title: List issues
tools.description: List issues (and pull requests, flagged) in a repository, newest first, up to 50 a page.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.get_issue
tools.title: Get issue
tools.description: Read one issue: title, body, state and labels.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.get_file
tools.title: Get file
tools.description: Read a file at a branch, tag or commit. Text up to 256 KiB comes back as is; anything larger or binary as a digest.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

path.description: A path inside the repository, like docs/x.md.

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit; default the default branch.

tools.name: github.list_prs
tools.title: List prs
tools.description: List pull requests in a repository, newest first, up to 50 a page.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.get_pr
tools.title: Get pr
tools.description: Read one pull request: title, body, head, base and merge state.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.create_issue
tools.title: Create issue
tools.description: Open an issue. Deedglass appends a hidden marker with the action id to the body.
tools.read_back: GitHub shows the issue with the same title, body and marker, opened by this connector's identity.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.comment
tools.title: Comment
tools.description: Comment on an issue or a pull request. Deedglass appends a hidden marker with the action id.
tools.read_back: The comment exists on issue n with the same body and marker.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.create_branch
tools.title: Create branch
tools.description: Create a branch from another branch or a commit (default: the default branch).
tools.read_back: The branch points at the requested commit.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

from.description: A branch name or a full commit SHA.

tools.name: github.create_or_update_file
tools.title: Create or update file
tools.description: Create or replace one text file on a branch in one commit. Send expected_sha to replace an existing file.
tools.read_back: The file's blob SHA on that branch equals the git blob SHA of the content Deedglass sent.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

path.description: A path inside the repository, like docs/x.md.

tools.name: github.create_pr
tools.title: Create pr
tools.description: Open a pull request from head into base. Deedglass appends a hidden marker with the action id to the body.
tools.read_back: The pull request is open from head into base with the same title and body.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.merge_pr
tools.title: Merge pr
tools.description: Merge a pull request. expected_head_sha is required: GitHub refuses the merge if the head moved.
tools.read_back: GitHub reports it merged, and the merge commit is contained in base.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.delete_branch
tools.title: Delete branch
tools.description: Delete a branch. The repository's default branch is never deleted.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

tools.name: github.close_issue
tools.title: Close issue
tools.description: Close an issue as completed or not planned.
tools.read_back: The issue is closed with that reason.

repo.description: owner/name; it must be in the connector's repos.

data.title: Gmail
data.description: Write and read drafts in one Gmail mailbox. No tool sends, and the connector can't reach a send endpoint, so people send drafts themselves. Every draft is read back from Gmail.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: The Desktop OAuth client's id. deedglass connector gmail authorize stores it.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Written by deedglass connector gmail authorize; never pasted by hand.

fields.name: service_account_json
fields.help: Google Workspace only: a service-account key with domain-wide delegation for gmail.compose.

auth.description: oauth (deedglass connector gmail authorize) or service_account (Google Workspace, domain-wide delegation).

mailbox.description: me, or with a service account the user to act as, like ops@acme.com.

internal_domains.description: Domains that count as inside your org, like acme.com.

allow_bcc.description: Default false: drafts with Bcc are refused.

api_base_url.description: https://gmail.googleapis.com (any http(s) URL in dev only)

token_url.description: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token (any http(s) URL in dev only)

data.summary: Drafts in one Gmail mailbox. People send them.

setup.title: Create a Google Cloud project
setup.detail: Enable the Gmail API, set the OAuth consent screen to External and Testing, and add yourself as a test user.

setup.title: Create a Desktop OAuth client
setup.detail: Credentials › Create credentials › OAuth client ID › Desktop app. Download the JSON and chmod 600 it.

setup.title: Authorize
setup.detail: Sign in with Google in the browser tab it opens. Apps in Testing need this again every 7 days.

limits: Drafts only. Nothing sends: people send drafts from Gmail.
Google's gmail.compose scope itself permits sending, so drafts only is enforced by Deedglass, not by Google.
No attachments, labels or deletes.
Google apps in Testing get 7-day refresh tokens: authorize again every week.

tools.name: gmail.create_draft
tools.title: Create draft
tools.description: Save a draft in the mailbox. It doesn't send: a person reviews and sends it from Gmail.
tools.read_back: The saved draft has the same recipients, subject and body.

to.description: Recipients, like "Priya <priya@acme.com>". Each entry is one address. At least 1. At most 20 recipients in all.

cc.description: Cc recipients. At most 20 recipients in all.

bcc.description: Bcc recipients (refused unless the connector allows Bcc). At most 20 recipients in all.

body_html.description: An optional HTML body. Stored as is; Deedglass never renders it.

thread_id.description: Put the draft in this thread.

in_reply_to.description: The Message-ID this replies to, like <abc@mail.gmail.com>.

tools.name: gmail.update_draft
tools.title: Update draft
tools.description: Replace a draft's recipients, subject and body. It doesn't send.
tools.read_back: The updated draft has the same recipients, subject and body.

to.description: Recipients, like "Priya <priya@acme.com>". Each entry is one address. At least 1. At most 20 recipients in all.

cc.description: Cc recipients. At most 20 recipients in all.

bcc.description: Bcc recipients (refused unless the connector allows Bcc). At most 20 recipients in all.

body_html.description: An optional HTML body. Stored as is; Deedglass never renders it.

thread_id.description: Put the draft in this thread.

in_reply_to.description: The Message-ID this replies to, like <abc@mail.gmail.com>.

tools.name: gmail.list_drafts
tools.title: List drafts
tools.description: List the mailbox's draft ids (at most 25).

tools.name: gmail.get_draft
tools.title: Get draft
tools.description: Read a draft: to, cc, subject, the plain-text body (up to 64 KiB) and the thread id.

tools.name: gmail.get_thread
tools.title: Get thread
tools.description: Read a thread: up to 20 messages, each body up to 16 KiB. Needs the gmail.readonly scope.

data.title: PostgreSQL
data.description: Agent SQL in a transaction Deedglass controls: one statement per action, run as the least-privilege role deedglass_agent, with a ledger row and a logical marker committed with the change for the witness.

allowed_schemas.description: the read scope and search_path, like [public]

writable_tables.description: schema.table the agent may INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE

auto_columns.description: table → columns a trigger maintains, like {public.orders: [updated_at]}

max_rows.description: table → the most rows one action may change

l2_timeout.description: how long an action waits for Postgres's change log, 1s to 60s (10s)

data.summary: Agent SQL in a controlled transaction, witnessed by Postgres's own change log.

setup.title: Create the connector
setup.command: deedglass connector create --type postgres --name pg-main --config pg-main.yaml

setup.title: Prepare the database
setup.detail: Review the plan, then apply it in one transaction.

limits: One statement per action, run as deedglass_agent.
L2 needs logical replication (wal_level logical) and a replication slot.
No DDL, COPY, DO blocks or session settings from agents.

tools.name: postgres.query
tools.title: Query
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement against  and get up to 500 rows back. Read-only: it never commits.

sql.description: One read-only SQL statement (SELECT). Use $1, $2 … for values.

params.description: Values for $1, $2 …: strings, integers, booleans or null; at most 100.

limit.description: Return at most this many rows (default and maximum 500).

tools.name: postgres.execute
tools.title: Execute
tools.description: Run one INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE in a transaction Deedglass controls, as a least-privilege role.
tools.read_back: Postgres's change log shows exactly the rows the statement changed (L2); the row read-back confirms them (L1).

sql.description: One INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. Use $1, $2 … for values.

params.description: Values for $1, $2 …: strings, integers, booleans or null; at most 100.

tools.name: postgres.describe
tools.title: Describe
tools.description: List the tables the agent can read: columns, types, primary keys, row estimates, and which tables are writable and watched.

data.title: REST API
data.description: Any JSON API as governed tools: one method on one templated path per tool, with the credential added only when the Gate runs a call.
data.summary: Any JSON API as governed tools, one method and path per tool.

setup.title: Describe the tools
setup.detail: One method on one templated path per tool, with an argument schema and, for writes, a read-back.

setup.title: Store the credential
setup.command: deedglass connector credentials set orders --from-env ORDERS_TOKEN

limits: Tools come from your config: Deedglass knows only what you describe.
L1 needs a read tool and a read-back in the config; without one, writes stay at L0.
JSON only. No streaming, uploads or redirects to other hosts.

data.title: Remote MCP server
data.description: A remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Its tools pass through the Gate; its credential stays in the vault and is added only when the Gate opens a session.

fields.name: value
fields.help: The value of the header the config names.

data.summary: A remote MCP server's tools, through the Gate.

setup.title: Create the connector
setup.detail: The server's URL and how it authenticates.
setup.command: deedglass connector create --type mcp_http --name my-mcp --config my-mcp.yaml

setup.title: Store the credential
setup.command: deedglass connector credentials set my-mcp --from-env MCP_TOKEN

limits: Tools come from the server. Their side effect is unknown: their annotations are the server's claim.
L0 only: Deedglass can't read an MCP server's writes back.

data.title: Slack
data.description: Post and react in allowed channels as a bot, read recent messages, and approve actions from Slack. Posts are read back through message metadata that carries the action id.

fields.name: bot_token
fields.help: The Bot User OAuth Token from the app's OAuth & Permissions page.

fields.name: signing_secret
fields.help: From the app's Basic Information page: 32 hex characters.

team_id.description: The workspace id, checked against auth.test.

app_id.description: From the app's Basic Information page, checked through bots.info.

channels.description: Channels the bot may post in: #name or a C… or G… id; ["*"] is any channel the bot is in.

read_channels.description: Channels the bot may read, in the same form.

api_base_url.description: https://slack.com/api (any http(s) URL in dev only)

data.summary: Posts, reactions and approvals in the Slack channels you allow.

setup.title: Create the Slack app from the manifest
Store the bot token and signing secret
setup.command: deedglass connector credentials set slack --field bot_token=env:SLACK_BOT_TOKEN --field signing_secret=env:SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET

limits: Only channels in the config, compared by id.
No direct messages to people, file uploads or message deletes.
Approvals map a Slack account to a person only by a confirmed email address.

tools.name: slack.list_channels
tools.title: List channels
tools.description: List the public and private channels the bot is in (at most 200).

tools.name: slack.read_channel
tools.title: Read channel
tools.description: Read recent messages of an allowed channel: ts, user, text (up to 4 KiB each) and thread_ts.

channel.description: #name, name, or a channel id (C… or G…).

limit.description: How many recent messages, at most 20.

tools.name: slack.post_message
tools.title: Post message
tools.description: Post a message as the bot in an allowed channel, optionally in a thread. Links are not unfurled.
tools.read_back: Slack shows the message in that channel with the same text and this action's id in its metadata.

channel.description: #name, name, or a channel id (C… or G…).

thread_ts.description: Reply in this thread (the parent message's ts).

tools.name: slack.add_reaction
tools.title: Add reaction
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction as the bot to a message in an allowed channel. A reaction already there counts as done.
tools.read_back: Slack lists the reaction on that message by this bot.

channel.description: #name, name, or a channel id (C… or G…).

name.description: The emoji name, like eyes or white_check_mark.

data.title: Stripe
data.description: Refunds, invoice items, customer metadata and subscription cancellations in a Stripe sandbox. Live keys are refused, every write carries the action id as its Idempotency-Key, and every write is read back from Stripe.

fields.name: token
fields.help: A restricted key from your Stripe sandbox.

api_version.description: Sent as Stripe-Version on every request. Default 2026-08-26.dahlia.

refund_limits.description: The most one refund may be, in minor units, per currency. Currencies not listed are refused. Each value is 1 to 99,999,999.

api_base_url.description: https://api.stripe.com (any http(s) URL in dev only)

data.summary: Refunds, invoice items and subscriptions in a Stripe sandbox.

setup.title: Create a restricted key
setup.detail: In your Stripe sandbox: Developers › API keys › Create restricted key. Don't tag it as an agent key: Deedglass is the approval surface.

setup.title: Store the key
setup.command: deedglass connector credentials set stripe --from-env STRIPE_TEST_KEY

limits: Sandbox only. Live keys are refused, and a live-mode answer disables the connector.
No payouts, transfers or payment creation.
No Stripe Connect accounts.
L1 shows Stripe's record, not whether the refund was right.
A refund Stripe holds for its own approval is UNVERIFIABLE: Deedglass can't see Stripe's reviewers.

tools.name: stripe.get_customer
tools.title: Get customer
tools.description: Read a customer: id, name, email and metadata.

tools.name: stripe.list_charges
tools.title: List charges
tools.description: List recent charges, optionally for one customer (at most 25).

starting_after.description: The last charge id of the previous page.

tools.name: stripe.get_charge
tools.title: Get charge
tools.description: Read a charge: amount, currency, what was refunded and whether it is disputed.

tools.name: stripe.get_payment_intent
tools.title: Get payment intent
tools.description: Read a PaymentIntent: amount, currency, status and its latest charge.

tools.name: stripe.list_refunds
tools.title: List refunds
tools.description: List the refunds of one charge or PaymentIntent (at most 25).

tools.name: stripe.get_subscription
tools.title: Get subscription
tools.description: Read a subscription: status, price per period and when the period ends.

tools.name: stripe.create_refund
tools.title: Create refund
tools.description: Refund part or all of a charge, in the charge's currency. Send charge or payment_intent, and amount in minor units.
tools.read_back: Stripe shows the refund for the same amount and currency on the same charge, status succeeded or pending.

payment_intent.description: Or the PaymentIntent to refund, pi_…

amount.description: Minor units of the charge's currency: 2000 is $20.00, 5000 is ¥5,000.

metadata.description: Up to 20 keys (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40 characters) with string values of at most 500 characters. Keys starting with deedglass_ are reserved.

tools.name: stripe.create_invoice_item
tools.title: Create invoice item
tools.description: Add an item to a customer's next invoice.
tools.read_back: Stripe shows the invoice item with the same amount, currency and customer.

amount.description: Minor units of the charge's currency: 2000 is $20.00, 5000 is ¥5,000.

metadata.description: Up to 20 keys (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40 characters) with string values of at most 500 characters. Keys starting with deedglass_ are reserved.

tools.name: stripe.update_customer_metadata
tools.title: Update customer metadata
tools.description: Set metadata keys on a customer. An empty string removes a key.
tools.read_back: Every key has the requested value, and deleted keys are gone.

metadata.description: Up to 20 keys (letters, digits, _ and -, at most 40 characters) with string values of at most 500 characters. Keys starting with deedglass_ are reserved.

tools.name: stripe.cancel_subscription
tools.title: Cancel subscription
tools.description: Cancel a subscription at the end of its period (the default), or at once with at_period_end false.
tools.read_back: Stripe shows the subscription canceled, or set to cancel at the period end.
